theory.mode: No modes - the chromatic scale contains all 12 pitches. It is completely symmetric: starting from any note produces the same intervallic content. Used as a technical resource and as a source of passing tones, not as a tonal framework.

relativeScale.name: No relative scale
relativeScale.relationship: Self-containing - includes all possible scales within it
relativeScale.intervalDistance: Every other scale is a subset of the chromatic scale; there is no relative key relationship

parallelScale.name: Major Scale (Ionian)
differences: Major scale selects 7 of 12 chromatic notes
Chromatic adds 5 additional passing tones between diatonic degrees

keyExamples.notes: C - C#/D♭ - D - D#/E♭ - E - F - F#/G♭ - G - G#/A♭ - A - A#/B♭ - B - C
keyExamples.accidentals: All sharps and flats are included
keyExamples.commonUse: Standard reference starting point, easiest to notate ascending with sharps and descending with flats

keyExamples.accidentals: All sharps and flats are included
keyExamples.commonUse: Common guitar starting point with open 5th string, standard for chromatic warm-up exercises

keyExamples.notes: E - F - F#/G♭ - G - G#/A♭ - A - A#/B♭ - B - C - C#/D♭ - D - D#/E♭ - E
keyExamples.accidentals: All sharps and flats are included
keyExamples.commonUse: Natural guitar starting point with open 6th string, ideal for full-range chromatic exercises

keyExamples.accidentals: All sharps and flats are included
keyExamples.commonUse: 3rd fret starting position on guitar, good for mid-neck chromatic exercises and warm-ups

patterns.description: Sequential half-step movement from open 6th string ascending fret by fret. The most fundamental guitar exercise pattern, covering every fret in first position.
Four-notes-per-string chromatic pattern starting at 5th fret. Builds finger independence and creates a moveable warm-up framework across the neck.

patterns.position: Single String (any string, full chromatic run)
patterns.description: Full chromatic run along a single string from open to 12th fret. Develops knowledge of all note names on each string and smooth position shifting.

commonPositions.usage: Fundamental warm-up exercises, finger strength and independence building
Four-finger chromatic drills, alternate picking exercises, mid-neck warm-ups
Upper fret chromatic exercises, smaller fret spacing for speed development

diatonicChords.function: The chromatic scale contains all 12 notes and therefore contains every possible chord. It has no diatonic harmony of its own - all chords are equally available.
Chromatic notes most commonly function as passing tones connecting diatonic chords by half step, creating smooth voice leading
diatonicChords.notes: Any half-step approach to a target chord tone

diatonicChords.function: Chords built on chromatic approach tones that resolve by half step into a diatonic target chord, used in jazz and classical
diatonicChords.notes: Half step above or below the target chord

diatonicChords.function: Chromatic notes above and below a target note used to surround and emphasize it, a core bebop jazz technique
diatonicChords.notes: Half step above and below the target

diatonicChords.function: Chromatic notes enable secondary dominant chords (V7 of any diatonic chord), the most common use of chromaticism in tonal music
diatonicChords.notes: Dominant 7th chord targeting any scale degree

diatonicChords.function: Chromatic diminished 7th chords used as passing chords between diatonic triads, connecting chords by half step in bass
diatonicChords.notes: Diminished 7th built on chromatic passing tones

commonProgressions.name: Chromatic Bass Descent (C - B/D# - Am - G#dim - C/G)
commonProgressions.description: Descending chromatic bass line from C to G using passing chromatic chords. One of the most common applications of chromaticism in tonal music.

commonProgressions.name: Secondary Dominant Chain (C - A7 - Dm - B7 - Em)
commonProgressions.description: Chain of secondary dominant chords using chromatic notes to create strong resolutions to each diatonic target chord in sequence.

commonProgressions.name: Jazz Chromatic Approach (D♭7 - Cmaj7)
commonProgressions.description: Chromatic approach from a half step above the target chord. Tritone substitution and chromatic approach are cornerstones of jazz harmony.

genreApplications.usage: Chromatic passing tones, enclosures, and approach notes are the foundation of bebop vocabulary, connecting chord tones with half-step movement
characteristics: bebop chromatic enclosures around chord tones
chromatic passing tones between scale degrees
examples: Charlie Parker - rapid chromatic bebop lines
Dizzy Gillespie - chromatic approach note vocabulary

genreApplications.usage: Chromatic passages for dramatic effect, chromatic voice leading, 12-tone serial composition, and technical etudes
characteristics: chromatic voice leading in Bach chorales
12-tone rows in Schoenberg and serial composers
virtuosic chromatic scale runs in concertos
examples: J.S. Bach - Chromatic Fantasy and Fugue

genreApplications.usage: Chromatic exercises are the foundation of guitar technique training for finger independence, speed, and coordination
characteristics: spider exercises and finger independence patterns

practiceExercises.name: Four-Finger Chromatic Warm-Up
practiceExercises.description: The fundamental chromatic exercise: play four consecutive frets on each string with one finger per fret, ascending across all six strings then descending
instructions: Start on the 6th string, play frets 1-2-3-4 with fingers 1-2-3-4, then move to the 5th string and repeat
Ascend across all six strings, then reverse the pattern descending from 1st string back to 6th
Use strict alternate picking and ensure every note rings cleanly before increasing tempo

practiceExercises.name: Chromatic Spider Exercise
practiceExercises.description: Finger permutation exercise using all 24 possible four-finger orderings across the chromatic scale to build complete finger independence
instructions: Start with pattern 1-2-3-4, then try 1-3-2-4, 1-4-2-3, and other permutations across the strings
Keep unused fingers hovering close to the fretboard to minimize unnecessary movement
Practice each permutation until it is clean and even before moving to the next

practiceExercises.name: Bebop Chromatic Enclosure Drill
practiceExercises.description: Practice chromatic enclosures around target chord tones, approaching from a half step above and below before landing on the target note
instructions: Choose a chord (e.g., Cmaj7) and target each chord tone with a chromatic enclosure from above and below
Practice enclosing the root, 3rd, 5th, and 7th of the chord in sequence across the fretboard
Apply over a jazz backing track, using enclosures to approach chord tones on strong beats

relatedScales.differences: Major scale selects 7 notes from the 12 chromatic tones using a specific whole-half step pattern; chromatic scale includes all 12
relatedScales.usage: Major scale provides tonal framework and hierarchy; chromatic scale provides passing tones and color between diatonic notes

relatedScales.differences: Whole tone selects every other chromatic note (6 of 12); both whole tone collections together equal the complete chromatic scale
relatedScales.usage: Whole tone creates a specific augmented color; chromatic is the raw material containing all possible colors

relatedScales.differences: Diminished scale alternates whole and half steps using 8 of 12 notes; chromatic uses all 12 with only half steps
relatedScales.usage: Diminished scale creates specific diminished chord harmony; chromatic is the universal superset
